22	## Node ownership — who authors the node
23	
24	Every node in a `.flow` file has exactly one author. The validator enforces this.
25

27	
28	| Category | Node types |
29	| --- | --- |

31	| Control flow | `core.logic.decision`, `core.logic.switch`, `core.logic.loop`, `core.logic.merge`, `core.control.end`, `core.logic.terminate`, `core.subflow` |

33	| Human-in-the-loop | `uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form` (inline form), `uipath.human-in-the-loop.coded-action-app` (app-based) |
34	| Patterns | `uipath.pattern.batch-transform`, `uipath.pattern.deep-rag` |

36	| Resource nodes | `uipath.core.rpa-workflow.*`, `uipath.core.agent.*`, `uipath.core.flow.*`, `uipath.core.agentic-process.*`, `uipath.core.api-workflow.*`, `uipath.core.human-task.*` |
37	| Document extraction | `uipath.ixp.*` — the extraction step must always land a node ([ixp/impl.md](references/plugins/ixp/impl.md#landing-the-node-when-you-cannot-fully-configure-it)) |

40	**CLI-owned nodes (`uip maestro flow node add` + `uip maestro flow node configure`):**
41	
42	| Category | Node types | Why |
43	| --- | --- | --- |
44	| Connector activities | `uipath.connector.<key>.<op>` | `inputs.detail` is a `=jsonString:essentialConfiguration` envelope. Validate rejects hand-authored shapes. |
45	| Connector triggers | `uipath.connector.trigger.<key>.<trigger>` | Same envelope + product-managed `bindings_v2.json` derivation. |
46	| Wait for events (mid-flow) | `uipath.connector.event.<key>.<event>` | Same envelope and event metadata as a trigger, but placed mid-flow (has an `input` port) instead of as the start node. See [connector-trigger/impl.md — Wait for events](references/plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md#wait-for-events-uipathconnectoreventkeyevent). |
47	| Managed HTTP | `core.action.http.v2` | Same envelope. |

49	For CLI-owned nodes:
50	
51	- Use `uip maestro flow node add` to insert the node and copy the definition into `definitions[]`.
52	- Use `uip maestro flow node configure --detail '{...}'` to populate `inputs.detail` and `bindings[]`.
53	- Subsequent edits to `inputs.detail` are also CLI-only — re-run `node configure` (it's a full rebuild; see [connector/impl.md](references/plugins/connector/impl.md)).
54	- **Never `Write` (full-file rewrite) a flow that contains CLI-owned nodes** — it silently clobbers their `bindings[]` / `inputs.detail`, leaving a corrupted connection binding that `flow validate` passes but `flow debug` fails on. `Edit` user-owned nodes in place; if a `Write` is unavoidable, re-run `node configure` for every CLI-owned node as the **last** write to touch `inputs.detail` / `bindings[]` (a later `Write` re-clobbers what `configure` just fixed).

56

59	## Critical rules
60	
61	1. **Always validate node types against the registry before building.** Use `registry search`/`list` for discovery and `registry get` for detailed metadata and definitions.
62	2. **ALWAYS follow the relevant plugin in [plugins/](references/plugins/) for every node type.** Each plugin has a `planning.md` (when to use, selection heuristics, ports) and `impl.md` (registry validation, JSON structure, CLI commands, configuration, debug). For connector nodes, the [connector](references/plugins/connector/impl.md) plugin covers connection binding, enriched metadata, and field resolution — required before building. Without this, node configuration will be wrong — errors that `flow validate` does not catch.
63	3. **Read the relevant Integration Service reference doc before any `uip is ...` call.** Two non-overlapping contracts:
64	   - **Read [/uipath:uipath-platform — connections.md](../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/connections.md) before any `uip is connections ...` call.** Applies to every connector activity, connector trigger, and managed HTTP node in connected mode. Single source of truth for command syntax, selection (including the personal-workspace auto-select rule), folder scoping, BYOA filtering, empty-result recovery, and ping verification. **If no healthy connection exists after following its recovery flow, STOP** and surface it in **Open Questions** during planning.
65	   - **Read [/uipath:uipath-platform — resources.md](../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/resources.md) before any `uip is resources run ...` call.** Applies to every reference-field lookup (Slack user IDs, Jira project keys, Outlook folder IDs, etc.). Single source of truth for the `Data.Pagination.HasMore` / `NextPageToken` contract and the `--query "nextPage=<token>"` loop. **Complete the pagination loop before reporting not-found** — do NOT abandon mid-loop to try alternative endpoints, `where=` filters the connector may not support, or asking the user. Plugin files cover node-specific configuration that follows connection binding: [connector/impl.md](references/plugins/connector/impl.md), [connector-trigger/impl.md](references/plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md), [http/impl-connector.md](references/plugins/http/impl-connector.md).
66	4. **Edit `<ProjectName>.flow` only** — other generated files (`bindings_v2.json`, `entry-points.json`, `operate.json`, `package-descriptor.json`) are managed by the CLI and may be overwritten. To declare flow inputs/outputs, add variables in the `.flow` file (see [shared/file-format.md](../shared/file-format.md)).
67	5. **`targetPort` is required on every edge** — `validate` rejects edges without it.
68	6. **Every node type needs a `definitions` entry** — copy from `uip maestro flow registry get <node-type>` output. Never hand-write definitions. The definition is the sole source for BPMN type (`model.type`), serviceType, event definitions, and binding/context templates — none of that belongs on the instance.
69	7. **Script nodes must `return` an object** — `return { key: value }`, not a bare scalar.
70	8. **Validate once at the end** — run `uip maestro flow validate` only after all nodes, edges, and configuration are complete. Do not validate after each individual node add or edit — intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
71	9. **Manage variables with `Edit` against the `.flow` file** — there are no CLI commands for variable management. Use `Edit` to add/remove/update entries in the `variables` section of the `.flow` file. See [shared/variables-and-expressions.md](../shared/variables-and-expressions.md).
72	10. **Every `out` variable must be mapped on every reachable End node** — missing output mappings cause runtime errors. See [shared/variables-and-expressions.md](../shared/variables-and-expressions.md).
73	11. **`=js:` prefix is REQUIRED on every `$vars`/`$metadata`/`$self` reference in a value field** — not on condition expressions (decision, switch, HTTP branch), which are auto-evaluated as JS. Without it, the BPMN runtime sees a literal string and `flow validate` fails with MST-9107. See [shared/node-output-wiring.md](../shared/node-output-wiring.md) for the canonical rule and per-node-type field reference, and [shared/variables-and-expressions.md](../shared/variables-and-expressions.md) for the expression system.
74	12. **Always run `flow format` after edits** — `uip maestro flow format <ProjectName>.flow` is the canonical layout step. Format arranges nodes horizontally, sets each node's `size` by its canvas shape (inline agents → 288×96, containers → 560×320, everything else → 96×96), and recurses into subflows (`subflows[<id>].layout`). Skipping format is the most common cause of misshapen nodes in Studio Web.
75	13. **Don't hand-write `layout.nodes` or `subflows[<id>].layout`** — these are owned by `flow format`. When authoring nodes, any placeholder `position` is fine (e.g. `{ x: 0, y: 0 }`); format rewrites it on save. Sticky notes (`type: "stickyNote"`) are the one exception — format preserves their custom size and position. See [shared/file-format.md — Layout](../shared/file-format.md#layout).
76	14. **Every data-producing node MUST have a matching `variables.nodes[]` entry — this is what makes `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` resolve.** The BPMN emitter walks `variables.nodes[]` to write the process-level `<uipath:inputOutput>` declarations the runtime needs. The instance `outputs` block is **only** consumed by BPMN serialization on end-style nodes (to map workflow-level `out` variables); for action / trigger nodes it is documentation, not behavior. Skipping `variables.nodes[]` produces a flow that passes `flow validate` but resolves `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` to `undefined` at runtime (MST-9972). **Always run `uip maestro flow format` after structural edits — it regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`** (matching what `uip maestro flow node add` and the canvas save path do), so this becomes self-healing as long as you `format`. See [shared/file-format.md — Node outputs](../shared/file-format.md#node-outputs).
77	15. **Node instances have no `model` block** — BPMN type, serviceType, version, event definitions, and binding/context templates live in the node's **definition** (in the top-level `definitions[]` array, copied verbatim from `registry get`). The runtime hydrates these from the definition at serialization time. Instance-specific identity fields live under `inputs`: `entryPointId`, `isDefaultEntryPoint` (triggers), `color`/`content` (sticky notes), and `source` (every inline-agent-related node — both `uipath.agent.autonomous` and every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node use `inputs.source = <UUID>`; their definitions declare `model.source: true` and flow-core hoists onto the instance).
78	16. **Error handling is off by default — never enable it on a node that handles no stated failure.** Leave `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` unset and add no `error` edge unless the requirements say what should happen when that node fails ("if the call fails…", "return X for invalid input", "handle timeouts"). An unhandled failure must fault the flow. When you do wire an `error` edge, it must reach a terminal the caller can distinguish from success — never the next happy-path node or the success End node. Without this, a failed run reports success. See [shared/file-format.md — Implicit error port on action nodes](../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes).
79	17. **Never invent the business meaning or format of a named output — elicit it.** When a request names an output (`caseKey`, `severity`, `status`, `ticketId`, …) but does not define how its value is derived, treat that as a business decision, not a coding choice — whether an identifier passes through unchanged or is reformatted (prefixed, combined, recomputed) is the user's rule to state, not yours to guess. Ask before building ([SKILL.md rule #5](../../SKILL.md#critical-rules-universal) — dropdown + "Something else"), or state your assumption explicitly and get confirmation. A guessed format produces a flow that passes `flow validate` yet returns the wrong value at runtime — the validator checks structure, never business correctness.

7	## Should you plan first?
8	
9	For complex flows, produce a plan before building. Reference [planning-arch.md](planning-arch.md) and [planning-impl.md](planning-impl.md) for the node type catalog, port reference, wiring rules, and topology patterns.
10

12	- The flow has 5+ nodes with branching or parallel paths
13	- The flow uses connectors or resources that need discovery
14	- The user's requirements are ambiguous and you need to confirm the approach

16	**Don't plan when:**
17	- Adding/editing a single node in an existing flow (use [brownfield.md](brownfield.md))

33	## Three-turn execution map
34	
35	Steps 0–6 are **logical phases**, not separate turns. A typical greenfield build collapses to **three assistant turns** (universal SKILL.md rule #10). Each step heading below carries a `[T1]` / `[T2]` / `[T3]` tag — emit every tool call inside the same Turn as one assistant message.
36	
37	| Turn | Steps | What you emit in ONE assistant message |
38	|---|---|---|
39	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-execution-map-intro:end-->
40	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t1-execution:start-->
41	| **T1 — Setup + discovery** | 0, 1, 2, 3 | One chained `Bash` (scaffold + register + pull + `node add` for each CLI-owned node) **+** parallel `Bash` (one `registry get` per OOTB type you'll inline) **+** parallel `Read` (plugin `impl.md`s). **If existing `.uipx` solutions are present, the Step 2 gate fires first in its own turn** — resolve it before this chain. |
42	| **T2 — Read + author** | 4 | One `Read` of the `.flow` **+** a batch of `Edit` calls (or one `Write` if ≥70% of nodes change). Claude Code serializes Edits on the same file, so they don't race |
43	| **T3 — Finalize** | 5, 6 | One chained `Bash` (`node configure && validate && format`). On validate failure: one Edit turn, then re-chain `validate && format` |
44	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t1-execution:end-->

46	### Batching anti-patterns
47	
48	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-init-batching:start-->
49	- **One CLI per turn.** Never issue `solution init`, then `cd`, then `flow init` as three separate Bash calls — chain with `&&`, the `cd` included as its own segment. Same for `node configure && validate && format`.
50	- **Sequential `registry get`s.** Emit every `registry get` as a parallel `Bash` in one message alongside the T1 scaffold chain.
51	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-init-batching:end-->
52	- **Validating after every Edit.** Validate once at the end of T3 (or after a recovery Edit). Intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
53	- **Re-reading the `.flow` every turn.** `Read` once at the start of T2; subsequent `Edit`s in the same conversation don't need re-reading unless an external command (e.g., `node configure`, `format`) rewrites the file between Edits.
54	- **`Edit` in the same turn as a `Bash` that mutates the same file.** Parallel tool calls race — separate them across turns.
55	- **Two parallel `Edit`s anchored to the same byte range.** Same-file Edits serialize in execution order; if Edit N's `old_string` overlaps text that Edit N-1's substitution removed or shifted, Edit N fails with "string not found." Use the [per-array anchor pattern](#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order) — anchor each Edit on its target array's own opening key, never on key order or a shared boundary.

85	## Step 2 — Create a solution, THEN a Flow project inside it **[T1]**
86	
87	> **A Flow project cannot exist outside a solution** (universal rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md)). Run `uip maestro flow init` (Step 2b) outside a solution and it now **auto-scaffolds** one — `<Project>Solution/<Project>Solution.uipx` with the project nested at `<Project>Solution/<Project>/` (response carries `Data.AutoCreatedSolution`). Still scaffold or select the solution first (Step 2a) so you set the solution name yourself rather than the auto `<Project>Solution`, and so discovery is unambiguous. The solution and project names are independent — they need not match. The correct layout is **always** `<Solution>/<Project>/<Project>.flow` (double-nested — see the tree after Step 2c). Passing `--skip-solution-registration` opts out of both auto-scaffold and registration, leaving a bare single-nested layout that fails Studio Web upload and packaging.
88	
89	Check for existing solutions with `find . -maxdepth 2 -type f -name '*.uipx' -print` (each solution is its own folder — `<Solution>/<Solution>.uipx` — so a bare `*.uipx` glob misses them). If any are found, **STOP before the T1 chain — do not run `uip solution init` yet** — and ask the user which solution to use per the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md) (rules #5 and #6): one option per discovered `.uipx`, a **"Create a new solution"** option, and **"Something else"** last. Rule #5 owns the ask mechanism (structured `AskUserQuestion` where the runtime offers it, a numbered chat list otherwise, recommended-option fallback when non-interactive) — do not re-specify a tool here. Applies even when the user wants a new solution. If none are found, create a new one automatically.

91	- If the user specifies an existing `.uipx` file path or solution name, use that (skip to Step 2b)
92	- Otherwise, create a new solution (Step 2a)

94	### Canonical T1 chain — issue this as ONE `Bash` call
95	
96	This is the consolidated command that does Steps 2a + 2b + Step 3 + (optionally) one `node add` per CLI-owned node, in one chained Bash. `node add` signature is `<file> <node-type>` (file first):
97	
98	```bash
99	uip solution init "<SolutionName>" --output json \
100	  && cd "<SolutionName>" \
101	  && uip maestro flow init "<ProjectName>" --output json \
102	  && cd "<ProjectName>" \
103	  && uip maestro flow registry pull \
104	  && uip maestro flow node add "<ProjectName>.flow" core.action.http.v2 --label "<NodeLabel>" --output json
105	```
106	
107	> **One creation path — never drop the `cd`.** `uip solution init "<SolutionName>"` → `cd "<SolutionName>"` → `uip maestro flow init "<ProjectName>"`, one chain. Without the `cd`, `flow init` runs in the old directory and auto-scaffolds a duplicate `<ProjectName>Solution/` (1-node husk). Never let auto-scaffold create the solution. Finish with exactly one `project.uiproj` — delete strays.
108	
109	Tail-append one `node add` per CLI-owned node (`uipath.connector.*`, `uipath.connector.trigger.*`, `core.action.http.v2`). Each `node add` returns the new node `id` in `Data` — capture it from the chained output for T2/T3. Drop the trailing `node add` segment when the flow is OOTB-only.
110	
111	In the SAME assistant message (parallel to this chain): emit one `Bash` per OOTB `registry get <NODE_TYPE>` you'll need in T2 (always `core.control.end` — see Step 4), and parallel `Read` calls for any plugin `impl.md`s you'll consult.
112	
113	> **Older `solution-tool` (< 1.0.0)** used `solution new` (see [.claude/rules/cli-renames.md](../../../../../.claude/rules/cli-renames.md)). If `solution init` returns `unknown command`, substitute `solution new`.

115	The sub-steps below describe what each command in the chain does and how to verify the result.
116	
117	### 2a. Create a new solution
118	
119	```bash
120	uip solution init "<SolutionName>" --output json
121	```
122	
123	Creates `<cwd>/<SolutionName>/<SolutionName>.uipx`. **`cd` into the new solution directory before Step 2b.**
124	
125	> **Naming convention:** In **pure greenfield** (no existing solutions), default the solution name to the project name unless the user specifies otherwise. When solutions already exist and the user chooses "Create a new solution", **ask for the new solution's name** — do not reuse the project name (SKILL.md rule #6). The two names are independent.

127	### 2b. Create the Flow project inside the solution folder
128	
129	```bash
130	cd <directory>/<SolutionName> && uip maestro flow init <ProjectName> --output json
131	```
132	
133	The `cd` puts the project inside the solution you just created. Skip it and `flow init` won't find that solution (discovery walks **up**, not down into `<SolutionName>/`) — it auto-scaffolds a **second, separate** `<ProjectName>Solution/` beside your empty `<SolutionName>/`, leaving two solutions. The project no longer single-nests, but `cd` first to land in the right one.
134	
135	> **Bash session state persists across tool calls.** This `cd` is **not scoped to one Bash invocation** — your cwd remains inside `<SolutionName>/` for every subsequent `Bash` call until you `cd` somewhere else. Plan the rest of Step 2 (and Steps 3–6) accordingly: either keep using paths relative to the solution dir, or anchor with `$(pwd)` / the absolute `Data.Path` returned by `flow init`. Do NOT prefix later commands with the original `<directory>/<SolutionName>/...` — that would resolve as `<SolutionName>/<directory>/<SolutionName>/...` and look like a layout bug when it isn't.
136	
137	`--output json` is required so Step 2c can inspect `Data.SolutionRegistration.Status` to confirm the project was auto-registered with the parent solution.
138	
139	### 2c. Verify the project is registered in the solution
140	
141	When `uip maestro flow init` is run from inside a solution directory (Step 2b), it **auto-registers** the project with the nearest parent `.uipx`. Run outside any solution, it **auto-scaffolds** `<Project>Solution/` and registers the project in it — the response then also carries `Data.AutoCreatedSolution` (`{ Name, Path, SolutionFile }`) and `Status: Registered`. Pass `--skip-solution-registration` to opt out of both (Status `OptedOut`, bare single-nested layout). The success envelope always reports the outcome in `Data.SolutionRegistration`:
142	
143	```json
144	{
145	  "Result": "Success",
146	  "Code": "FlowInit",
147	  "Data": {
148	    "Status": "Created successfully",
149	    "Path": ".../<SolutionName>/<ProjectName>",
150	    "SolutionRegistration": {
151	      "Status": "Registered",                     // or "AlreadyRegistered"
152	      "Solution": ".../<SolutionName>.uipx",
153	      "Project": "<ProjectName>/project.uiproj",
154	      "ProjectId": "<uuid>"
155	    }
156	  }
157	}
158	```
159	
160	If `Data.SolutionRegistration.Status` is `Registered` or `AlreadyRegistered`, **you are done** with this step — proceed to the layout check. If it is `OptedOut`, you passed `--skip-solution-registration` and the skip was intentional.
161	
162	**Fallback** — when `Status` is `Skipped` (ambiguous discovery — e.g. multiple `.uipx`), `Failed` (the `.uipx` write failed), or `NotInSolution` (rare — auto-scaffold did not run and no parent `.uipx` was found): wire the project manually.

165	uip solution projects add \
166	  <directory>/<SolutionName>/<ProjectName> \
167	  <directory>/<SolutionName>/<SolutionName>.uipx
168	```

176	└── <SolutionName>/                    ← from `uip solution init`
177	    ├── <SolutionName>.uipx
178	    └── <ProjectName>/                 ← from `uip maestro flow init` (run from inside <SolutionName>/)

260	## Step 4 — Build the flow **[T2]**
261	
262	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-build-scaffold-assumptions:start-->
263	> **`flow init` scaffolds ONLY the manual trigger (`start` / `core.trigger.manual`) with zero edges.** Every other user-owned node — **including the End node** — is yours to add via `Edit` / `Write`. Any HTTP / connector / connector-trigger node you `node add`-ed in T1 is already in `nodes[]` and `definitions[]` but has empty `inputs.detail` (filled in T3) and is not wired yet.
264	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-build-scaffold-assumptions:end-->
265	
266	### T2 batch — issue these in ONE assistant message
267	
268	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t2-read-source:start-->
269	1. **One `Read`** of `<ProjectName>.flow` — required before any Edit/Write; T1's chained Bash mutated the file and Claude Code's file-state tracker does not auto-refresh on external mutations.
270	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t2-read-source:end-->
271	2. **A batch of parallel `Edit` calls** — one per top-level array you're modifying. Same-file Edits serialize in execution order, so each `old_string` must anchor to text NO OTHER parallel Edit modifies. Use the **per-array anchor pattern** below.
272	   - Edit `nodes[]` — add the End node (and any other user-owned nodes).
273	   - Edit `definitions[]` — paste the End definition verbatim from T1's `registry get core.control.end` output.
274	   - Edit `edges[]` — wire `trigger → <httpNode> → end`. End-node `outputs` mapping goes here too if you declared an `out` variable in `variables.globals`.
275	   - Edit `layout.nodes` — placeholder `{ position: { x: 0, y: 0 }, size: { width: 96, height: 96 }, collapsed: false }` per new node; `format` rewrites both position and size (by node shape) in T3.
276	
277	   `Write` of the whole file is allowed but token-costly on flows >~10 nodes — only fall back to `Write` when ≥70% of nodes change AND the file is small (see [editing-operations.md — Tool Selection Ladder](editing-operations.md#tool-selection-ladder)). **Never `Write` a flow that already has connector / connector-trigger / managed-HTTP nodes** — the rewrite clobbers their CLI-owned `bindings[]` / `inputs.detail` (invisible to `flow validate`); `Edit` in place, or re-run `node configure` as the last write. See [CAPABILITY.md — Node ownership](../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node).
278	
279	#### Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits — anchor on what you Read, not on key order
280	
281	> **Do not assume a top-level key order.** The CLI does not guarantee which keys are present or in what sequence — fixtures show `runtime` before `nodes` on one flow and absent on another, and `bindings` / `variables` / `solutionId` / `projectId` / `metadata` appear in varying positions. Any anchor of the form "closing `]` + the NEXT top-level key" is coupled to that ordering and will silently break across CLI versions or between flows. **Anchor on the target array's OWN key instead — you just `Read` the file at the top of T2, so anchor to text that read actually contains.**
282	
283	Anchor each Edit using its target array's own opening key, located in the text you just Read — not adjacency to a neighbor key. The catch: `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT unique in the file. They recur **inside inline `definitions[]`** (an HTTP v2 / agent / subprocess definition embeds its own nested `nodes`/`edges`) **and inside any `subflows.<id>` block** (each subflow holds its own `nodes`/`edges`) — so even a small flow can carry several copies. The reliable, version-independent discriminator is **indentation: the top-level array sits at 2-space indent; every nested one is deeper.** `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` appear once each, so they need no disambiguation.
284	
285	| Edit target | Anchor on (from the text you Read) | How to insert |
286	|---|---|---|
287	| Append to `nodes[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "nodes": [` (the top-level array — deeper-indented `"nodes": ["` inside definitions do not match the two-leading-space prefix) plus the `start` node's opening `{ "id": "start"`. | Insert the new node object as the first element, immediately after the `[`: `\n    { new node JSON },`. Head-insertion keeps `old_string` clear of the array's closing `]`. |
288	| Append to `edges[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "edges": [`. A newly generated scaffold commonly has `\n  "edges": []`; the 2-space prefix distinguishes it from nested `edges` arrays. | When empty, replace `\n  "edges": []` with `\n  "edges": [\n    { new edge JSON }\n  ]`. When non-empty, anchor through the first edge and insert the new edge as the first element. |
289	| Append to `definitions[]` | `"definitions": [` plus the first definition's opening bytes. Top-level `definitions[]` is the only one in the file, so this is reliably unique. | Insert the new definition right after the opening `[`, as the first element. Never anchor on whatever key follows `definitions` — that key varies (`runtime`, `bindings`, `variables`, `layout`, depending on CLI version and what the flow contains). |
290	| Add an entry to `layout.nodes` | `"layout": {\n    "nodes": {\n      "start":` — `start` is the always-present trigger and the first key under `layout.nodes` in newly generated flows. The top-level `"layout": {` is the only one. | `"layout":` + `"start":` jointly disambiguate. Insert `"<newId>": { ... },\n      ` before `"start":`. CLI-owned nodes added via `node add` already have a `layout.nodes` entry — only add entries for nodes you author by hand (e.g. End). |
291	
292	**Why head-insertion.** Inserting the new element right after the array's opening `[` means the `old_string` never includes the array's closing `]` — so it cannot collide with a closing `]` from a nested object (`form.sections[].fields[]`), and it never references a sibling top-level key whose position is not guaranteed. JSON array element order is not semantically significant for `nodes` / `edges` / `definitions`, so head vs. tail insertion is equivalent; `flow format` normalizes layout regardless.
293	
294	**Disjointness rule.** Two parallel Edits MUST anchor on DIFFERENT top-level arrays — nodes-Edit on the top-level `nodes[]`, edges-Edit on the top-level `edges[]`, definitions-Edit on `definitions[]`, layout-Edit on `layout.nodes`. Because each anchors on its own array (not a shared boundary), the parallel Edits never overlap — provided each anchor is unique first (see below).
295	
296	**Pre-flight uniqueness check.** Before submitting an Edit, confirm your `old_string` appears **exactly once** in the file you Read. `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` are reliably unique. `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT — they recur inside inline definitions and subflows, so anchor on the **2-space-indented** occurrence and extend through the first element's opening (e.g. `"id": "start"`) until the match count is one. Never anchor on a bare bracket shape, and never assume the first textual occurrence is the top-level one.
297	
298	**Safer fallback when in doubt:** serialize the Edits across two turns. One extra turn is cheaper than a failed-Edit recovery loop (which forces a re-Read, a re-derived anchor, and a re-submit).
299	
300	See [shared/file-format.md — Top-level structure](../../shared/file-format.md#top-level-structure) for which top-level keys exist and the note that their order is not guaranteed.
301	
302	> **Intra-turn ordering.** If a parallel `Edit` fails with "file not read," split `Read` into its own turn (cost: +1 turn).

1	# Connector Activity Nodes — Planning
2	
3	Connector activity nodes call external services (Jira, Slack, Salesforce, Outlook, etc.) via UiPath Integration Service. They are dynamically loaded — not built-in — and appear in the registry after `uip login` + `uip maestro flow registry pull`.
4	
5	## When to Use
6	
7	Use a connector activity node when the flow needs to **call an external service that has a pre-built UiPath connector**. Connectors handle auth (OAuth, API keys), token refresh, and error formatting automatically at runtime. Note: design-time reference resolution (looking up records by name during authoring) still requires the agent to paginate — see [impl.md](impl.md).
8	
9	### Decision Order
10	
11	Prefer higher tiers when connecting to external services:
12	
13	| Tier | Approach | When to Use |
14	| --- | --- | --- |
15	| 1 | **IS connector activity** (this node type) | A connector exists and its activities cover the use case |
16	| 2 | **Managed HTTP Request** (`core.action.http.v2`) | A connector exists but lacks the specific curated activity — uses the connector's IS connection for auth |
17	| 3 | **Managed HTTP Request — manual mode** (`core.action.http.v2`) | No connector exists — you provide the full URL manually |
18	| 4 | **RPA workflow** | Target system has no API at all (legacy desktop apps, terminals) |
19	
20	### Prerequisites
21	
22	- `uip login` required — connector nodes only appear in the registry after authentication
23	- A healthy IS connection must exist for the connector — if none exists, the user must create one before proceeding
24	- `uip maestro flow registry pull` must be run to cache connector node types locally
25	
26	### When NOT to Use
27	
28	- **No connector exists for the service** — use `core.action.http.v2` manual mode instead
29	- **Simple GET request with no auth** — `core.action.http.v2` (manual mode) is simpler and faster to configure
30	- **The operation needs desktop/browser interaction** — use an RPA resource node
31	- **The task requires reasoning or judgment** — use an agent node
32	
33	## Node Type Pattern
34	
35	`uipath.connector.<connector-key>.<activity>`
36	
37	Examples:
38	- `uipath.connector.uipath-salesforce-slack.send-message`
39	- `uipath.connector.uipath-atlassian-jira.create-issue`
40	
41	## Discovery
42	
43	```bash
44	uip maestro flow registry search <service> --output json \
45	  --output-filter "[*].{NodeType:NodeType,DisplayName:DisplayName,Description:Description,AvailableOnTenant:AvailableOnTenant}"
46	```
47	
48	`registry search` returns `Data` as a flat array, and each row uses PascalCase fields (`NodeType`, `DisplayName`, `Description`, `AvailableOnTenant`). Do **not** parse `Data.Nodes`, lowercase `type`, or lowercase `category`; those shapes do not exist in the CLI JSON output.
49	
50	For connector activities, use `NodeType` as the source of truth:
51	
52	- Activity rows start with `uipath.connector.<connector-key>.`
53	- Trigger rows start with `uipath.connector.trigger.` and belong to the connector-trigger guide
54	- `NodeType` is the exact value to pass to `registry get` and `node add`
55	- `Category` can be tenant/internal metadata such as `connector.<id>` and is not a reliable connector-key source
56	
57	If the connector key fails, list all connectors:
58	
59	```bash
60	uip is connectors list --output json
61	```
62	
63	Keys are often prefixed — e.g., `uipath-salesforce-slack` not `slack`.
64	
65	### Sanity-check before deciding "no connector activity exists"
66	
67	A `registry search <service>` that returns **only `uipath.connector.trigger.*`** entries — zero activity entries — is **suspicious, not authoritative**. Connector activities and triggers are independent fetches against different typecache endpoints; the registry cache can transiently miss the activity branch when one of those endpoints flakes (TTL: 30 min). Falling through to managed HTTP at this point produces a flow that *validates* but skips the real connector node — a silent topology mistake.
68	
69	When `registry search` returns triggers but **no activities** for a service whose connector you've already confirmed exists (`uip is connectors list`), or returns nothing at all for a well-known connector, **force a fresh pull before falling back**:
70	
71	```bash
72	uip maestro flow registry pull --force
73	uip maestro flow registry search <service> --output json
74	```
75	
76	If the second search still returns no activities for that connector, the fallback to managed HTTP (Tier 2 below) is legitimate. If the second search now lists activities, the cache was stale — proceed with the connector activity node as Tier 1.
77	
78	> **Why this matters**: a partial registry pull is an indirect failure — `registry pull` reports `Success` even when one node-source branch silently dropped its contribution. The shape (`triggers > 0 && activities == 0`) is the only local signal you have. Treat it like a stale-cache symptom, not a topology fact.
79	
80	### Disambiguation — when search returns multiple connectors for the same intent
81	
82	`uip maestro flow registry search <keyword>` routinely returns multiple connectors for the same user intent (e.g. searching `databricks` returns both the native AI-serving connector and the JDBC gateway). **Never silently pick the first match.**
83	
84	Apply the canonical disambiguation ladder owned by Integration Service:
85	
86	- [/uipath:uipath-platform — Integration Service — connectors.md — Connector Disambiguation](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/connectors.md#connector-disambiguation) — classify catalog/custom/mock, intent-match by `Description`, count remaining candidates (1 → silent, >1 → AskUser, 0 catalog → STOP).
87	- [/uipath:uipath-platform — Integration Service — connectors.md — JDBC Gateway — Database SQL Intent](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/connectors.md#jdbc-gateway--database-sql-intent) — special handling when the user's intent is a database SQL operation (native connector vs JDBC gateway, connection-name keyword matching, decision matrix, lifecycle disclosure).
88	
89	Lock the chosen connector key in the planning notes — never re-derive per node within the same flow.
90	
91	### Check Connector Connections
92	
93	For each connector found in registry search, verify a healthy connection exists. Extract the connector key from the node type name (e.g., `uipath.connector.uipath-microsoft-outlook365.get-newest-email` -> key is `uipath-microsoft-outlook365`).
94	
95	**Never type a connector key from memory.** Use the key from the `registry search` node type only. The registry key is frequently prefixed or qualified differently than the service's brand name (e.g. an Outlook connector keys as `uipath-microsoft-outlook365`, not `outlook`), so a guessed key silently misses the real connector and makes `connections list` return a false "No connections found."
96	
97	```bash
98	uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --all-folders --output json
99	```
100	
101	> `--all-folders` is mandatory. Without it the CLI returns the active folder only and hides connections in other folders the user can see. Plain `uip is connections list "<connector-key>"` is forbidden for discovery.
102	
103	- If a default enabled connection exists (`IsDefault: Yes`, `State: Enabled`), record the connection ID for implementation planning.
104	- **If the result is empty, do not conclude "no connection exists."** An empty `connections list` is suspicious, not authoritative. Three things must hold before you treat it as real: (a) the key came from `registry search`, not memory; (b) the call used `--all-folders`; (c) a `--refresh` retry was still empty. Only then surface it in **Open Questions** so the user can create one while reviewing. Never ask the user a connection-creation question on an unverified empty result. See [impl.md](impl.md) for the platform-skill empty-result recovery path shared with implementation.
105	
106	## Ports
107	
108	| Input Port | Output Port(s) |
109	| --- | --- |
110	| `input` | `success`, `error` |
111	
112	The `error` port is the implicit error port shared with all action nodes — see [Implicit error port on action nodes](../../../../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes).
113	
114	## Output Variables
115	
116	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output` — the connector response (structure depends on the operation)
117	- `$vars.{nodeId}.error` — error details if the call fails
118	
119	## HTTP Fallback (Managed HTTP Request)
120	
121	When a connector exists but lacks the specific curated activity, use `core.action.http.v2` (Managed HTTP Request). This node proxies through the `uipath-uipath-http` connector and uses the **target connector's** IS connection for authentication — you supply the API URL and payload.
122	
123	> **Do NOT use individual connector HTTP request nodes** (e.g., `uipath.connector.<key>.http-request`). Always use the unified `core.action.http.v2` Managed HTTP Request node for non-curated API calls.
124	
125	> **Do NOT use `core.action.http` (v1) with `authenticationType: "connection"` for this.** The v1 node does not pass IS credentials at runtime. Always use `core.action.http.v2`.
126	
127	See [http/planning.md](../http/planning.md) for full selection heuristics and [http/impl.md](../http/impl.md) for configuration via `uip maestro flow node configure`.
128	
129	Note as `managed-http: <service> — <operation>` during planning.
130	
131	## Planning Annotation
132	
133	In the architectural plan, annotate connector nodes as:
134	- `connector: <service-name>` with the intended operation (e.g., "connector: Jira — create issue")
135	- If discovery found no connector, fall back to `core.action.http.v2` (manual mode) or flag the gap in Open Questions

1	# Operate — Ship, run, and manage deployed flows
2	
3	<!--skill-flavor:upload-operate-intro:start-->
4	Capability index for the lifecycle of a flow as a deployed asset. Operate owns everything that touches the cloud — `solution resources refresh`, Studio Web upload, Orchestrator deploy, `flow debug`, `process run`, `job status/traces`, and `instance` lifecycle (pause, resume, cancel, retry). Requires `uip login`.
5	<!--skill-flavor:upload-operate-intro:end-->
6	
7	> **Where you came from / where to go next.** Operate is downstream of Author (build the flow → ship it) and upstream of Diagnose (run faults → diagnose). Build/edit lives in [author/CAPABILITY.md](../author/CAPABILITY.md); fault triage lives in [diagnose/CAPABILITY.md](../diagnose/CAPABILITY.md).
8	>
9	> **Inherits universal rules from [SKILL.md](../../SKILL.md)** — `--output json` + prefer `--output-filter` for extraction, no `flow debug` without consent, never invoke other skills automatically, dropdown question pattern, solution layout, **plain-English narration + granular progress list (opt-in — silent by default; engage when the user asks for verbosity)**. The rules below are operate-scoped and apply on top.
10	
11	## When to use this capability
12	
13	<!--skill-flavor:upload-scope-bullets:start-->
14	- Push a flow to Studio Web (`uip solution upload`)
15	- Deploy a flow to Orchestrator (`uip maestro flow pack` + `uip solution publish`)
16	<!--skill-flavor:upload-scope-bullets:end-->
17	- Run a flow end-to-end via `uip maestro flow debug` (cloud round-trip with real side effects)
18	- Trigger a deployed process via `uip maestro flow process run`
19	- Check job status or stream traces with `uip maestro flow job status` / `job traces`
20	- Manage a running instance — pause, resume, cancel, or retry
21	- Refresh solution resources after binding changes (`uip solution resources refresh`)
22	
23	## Critical rules
24	
25	<!--skill-flavor:upload-refresh-rule:start-->
26	1. **Always run `uip solution resources refresh --solution-folder <SolutionDir>` before `solution upload` or `flow debug`.** Stale resource declarations cause runtime binding failures even when the local `.flow` is correct. The refresh syncs connection and process resource declarations from the project's `bindings_v2.json` files into the solution. `refresh` has no positional solution argument; omit `--solution-folder` only when the current directory is already the solution root.
27	<!--skill-flavor:upload-refresh-rule:end-->
28	<!--skill-flavor:upload-publish-default-rule:start-->
29	2. **Default to Studio Web when the user says "publish" without specifier.** "Publish" → `uip solution upload <SolutionDir>`. Only run `uip maestro flow pack` + `uip solution publish` when the user explicitly asks to deploy to Orchestrator. Pass the exact solution root path (the directory containing the `.uipx` file), or `.` when already in that directory; do not pass the solution name while the shell is inside a nested project folder. The Orchestrator path bypasses Studio Web — the user cannot visualize or edit the flow there.
30	<!--skill-flavor:upload-publish-default-rule:end-->
31	3. **Always include `--folder-key <FOLDER_KEY>` (`-f` shorthand) on `instance` commands.** Without it the command rejects the request before reaching the API. Get the folder key from `uip or folders list --output json` or from the job/process context. See [shared/cli-conventions.md](../shared/cli-conventions.md#6---folder-key-requirement).
32	4. **Always report Studio Web URL and Instance ID as the first two lines of any debug summary.** Parse `Data.studioWebUrl` and `Data.instanceId` from the JSON output. Use `<not returned by CLI>` if missing — never omit the line. Users need these immediately, not buried below status text.
33	
34	## Workflow
35	
36	| Journey | Read |
37	| --- | --- |
38	<!--skill-flavor:ship-journey-row:start-->
39	| Publish a flow (Studio Web default, Orchestrator on request) | [ship.md](references/ship.md) |

41	| Run a flow on demand or check progress | [run.md](references/run.md) |
42	| Intervene in a running instance | [manage.md](references/manage.md) |
43	
44	## Common tasks
45	
46	| I need to... | Read these |
47	| --- | --- |
48	<!--skill-flavor:ship-common-tasks-rows:start-->
49	| **Publish a flow to Studio Web** | [ship.md — Path 1](references/ship.md#path-1--studio-web-upload-default) |
50	| **Deploy a flow to Orchestrator** (only if explicitly requested) | [ship.md — Path 2](references/ship.md#path-2--orchestrator-deploy-explicit-only) + [/uipath:uipath-solution](/uipath:uipath-solution) |
51	| **Sync solution resource declarations** | [ship.md — Pre-flight](references/ship.md#pre-flight) (the `uip solution resources refresh` step) |
52	<!--skill-flavor:ship-common-tasks-rows:end-->
53	| **Debug a flow end-to-end** | [run.md — Debug](references/run.md#debug--controlled-end-to-end-run) |
54	| **Pass input arguments to `flow debug`** | [run.md — Debug](references/run.md#debug--controlled-end-to-end-run) (the `--inputs` flag) |
55	| **Bind local files to file-typed inputs** | [run.md — Debug](references/run.md#debug--controlled-end-to-end-run) and [run.md — Process run](references/run.md#process-run--trigger-a-deployed-process) (same `--attachment <variableId>=<localPath>` flag on both, repeatable; `--attachment` overrides `--inputs` on key collisions) |
56	| **Trigger a deployed process** | [run.md — Process run](references/run.md#process-run--trigger-a-deployed-process) |
57	| **Check status of a running job** | [run.md — Job inspection](references/run.md#job-inspection--status-and-traces) |
58	| **Stream verbose execution traces** | [run.md — Job inspection](references/run.md#job-inspection--status-and-traces) (use sparingly — see [diagnose/CAPABILITY.md](../diagnose/CAPABILITY.md)) |
59	| **Pause a running instance** | [manage.md](references/manage.md) |
60	| **Resume a paused instance** | [manage.md](references/manage.md) |
61	| **Cancel an instance** | [manage.md](references/manage.md) |
62	| **Retry a faulted instance** | [manage.md](references/manage.md) (after diagnosing root cause via [diagnose/CAPABILITY.md](../diagnose/CAPABILITY.md)) |
63	| **Look up `solution` / `flow pack` / `flow debug` / `process` / `job` / `instance` CLI syntax** | [shared/cli-commands.md](../shared/cli-commands.md) |
64	| **My flow run failed** | [diagnose/CAPABILITY.md](../diagnose/CAPABILITY.md) |
65	
66	## Anti-patterns
67	
68	<!--skill-flavor:upload-antipatterns:start-->
69	- **Never run `solution upload` without `solution resources refresh` first.** Stale resource declarations cause runtime binding failures.
70	- **Never default to Orchestrator deploy when the user said "publish".** "Publish" → Studio Web upload. Confirm explicitly before running `flow pack` + `solution publish`.
71	<!--skill-flavor:upload-antipatterns:end-->
72	- **Never run `flow debug` as a validation step.** Use `uip maestro flow validate` for correctness checking; debug is for end-to-end execution against real systems.

74	- **Never start diagnosis from `job traces`.** Traces are last-resort verbose output. Begin with incidents — see [diagnose/CAPABILITY.md](../diagnose/CAPABILITY.md) for the priority ladder.

1	# HTTP Request Node — Implementation
2	
3	This page is the entry point for implementing a managed HTTP node. Pick your auth mode below, then follow the matching walkthrough end-to-end. The "Shared Reference" section is an appendix — the mode walkthroughs already inline what you need to act, and link here only for full rationale and extended examples.
4	
5	## Node Type
6	
7	`core.action.http.v2` (Managed HTTP Request)
8	
9	> **Always use `core.action.http.v2`** for all HTTP requests. The older `core.action.http` (v1) is deprecated.
10	
11	## Pick a Mode
12	
13	| Mode | Use when | Walkthrough |
14	| --- | --- | --- |
15	| **Connector** | Target system has an IS connector — auth via an existing IS connection (OAuth/API key) | [impl-connector.md](impl-connector.md) |
16	| **Manual** | No connector exists, public/no-auth API, or quick prototyping | [impl-manual.md](impl-manual.md) |
17	
18	> **Mode fallback — auto-try, then confirm.** Prefer a curated connector activity first; if none, use connector mode; if connector mode cannot be configured (connector lacks HTTP request support — `HasHttpRequest` false — or no usable IS connection), fall through to manual mode automatically. Manual changes the auth model (you supply auth yourself), so confirm the switched mode with the user before finalizing. See [impl-connector.md — Step 2](impl-connector.md#step-2--identify-target-connection).
19	
20	The `--detail` payload differs in two places between modes: `authentication` (`"connector"` vs `"manual"`), and the connector-binding fields `targetConnector` / `connectionId` / `folderKey` (connector mode only; `url` is then relative to the connector base, vs. an absolute URL in manual mode). Everything else (node add, dynamic values, branches, edges, debug) is shared.
21	
22	## Critical: Use `node configure`
23	
24	> **Do not hand-write `inputs.detail`, `bindings_v2.json`, or connection resource files.** Run `uip maestro flow node configure` — it builds everything from a simple `--detail` JSON. Hand-written configurations miss the `essentialConfiguration` block and fail at runtime. `core.action.http.v2` is CLI-owned per [Author capability — Node ownership](../../../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node) (same envelope rules as connector activities).
25	
26	## Registry validation
27	
28	```bash
29	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.http.v2 --output json
30	```
31	
32	Confirm in `Data.Node.handleConfiguration`: target port `input`, source ports `branch-{item.id}` (dynamic, `repeat: inputs.branches`) and `default`. Also confirm `Data.Node.supportsErrorHandling: true` — HTTP v2 participates in the implicit `error` port pattern shared by every action node (see [Action Node Structure](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md)). Model `serviceType` is `Intsvc.UnifiedHttpRequest`.
33	
34	---
35	
36	## Shared Reference (appendix)
37	
38	The mode walkthroughs link into the sections below for full rationale and extended examples. You do not need to read this section in order — jump directly from the walkthrough link that brought you here.
39	
40	### Add the node
41	
42	```bash
43	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
44	  --label "<HTTP node label>" --output json
45	```
46	
47	The CLI copies the manifest into `definitions[]`, adds the node instance to `nodes[]`, registers the `variables.nodes` entries, and inserts a placeholder in `layout.nodes` — all in code, byte-for-byte from the registry (including `typeVersion`, which the CLI pulls from the manifest's `version` field; do not hardcode it). Save the returned node ID — both walkthroughs reuse it.
48	
49	The CLI initializes `inputs` from the manifest's `inputDefaults`:
50	
51	```json
52	"inputs": {
53	  "branches": [],
54	  "timeout": "PT15M",
55	  "retryCount": 0,
56	  "swaggerDefinition": null,
57	  "detail": {}
58	}
59	```
60	
61	`inputs.detail` is populated by the configure step (next). The inputs-level siblings — `branches`, `timeout`, `retryCount` — are set at `node add` time via `--input`:
62	
63	```bash
64	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
65	  --label "<HTTP node label>" \
66	  --input '{
67	    "timeout": "PT30M",
68	    "retryCount": 3,
69	    "branches": [
70	      { "id": "hasItems", "name": "Has Items", "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length > 0" },
71	      { "id": "empty",    "name": "Empty",    "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length == 0" }
72	    ]
73	  }' --output json
74	```
75	
76	- `timeout` — ISO 8601 duration (e.g. `PT15M`, `PT1H`, `P1D`). Default `PT15M`.
77	- `retryCount` — integer. Default `0`.
78	- `branches` — see [Conditional branches](#conditional-branches) below.
79	
80	> **Do not hand-author the `core.action.http.v2` definition, and do not `Edit` `inputs.*` after the fact.** Use `uip maestro flow node add` (with `--input` for branches/timeout/retryCount) and `uip maestro flow node configure` (for `inputs.detail`). These are the only supported authoring paths.
81	
82	### Dynamic values in URL / headers / body / query
83	
84	**IS activity input fields do not resolve `{$vars.x}` brace-templates.** The flow runtime's `{...}` template interpolation only applies to native flow fields (end-node output `source`, variable updates, decision `expression`, script body, etc.) — **not** to fields under `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on HTTP v2 or on any `uipath.connector.*` activity. Evidence: `"url": "https://.../user/{$vars.article}/..."` ships to the service as literal `{vars.article}` (the `$` is stripped, braces remain), producing a 400 Bad Request.
85	
86	**Use `=js:` expressions for any dynamic value in IS activity inputs.** The runtime evaluates `=js:` before handing the value to the connector:
87	
88	```json
89	"bodyParameters": {
90	  "url": "=js:`https://api.example.com/users/${$vars.userId}/orders`",
91	  "headers": {
92	    "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.apiToken",
93	    "X-Request-ID": "=js:$metadata.instanceId"
94	  },
95	  "query": {
96	    "since": "=js:$vars.startDate"
97	  }
98	}
99	```
100	
101	Template literals with `${...}` interpolation work because the whole expression is evaluated as JavaScript — `$vars` is a global in the `=js:` context. Plain string concatenation (`'Bearer ' + $vars.token`) works the same way.
102	
103	When calling `uip maestro flow node configure --detail`, pass the `=js:` string verbatim — the CLI stores it in `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` unchanged:
104	
105	```bash
106	uip maestro flow node configure <Project>.flow <nodeId> \
107	  --detail '{
108	    "authentication": "manual",
109	    "method": "GET",
110	    "url": "=js:`https://api.example.com/users/${$vars.userId}`"
111	  }' --output json
112	```
113	
114	### Conditional branches
115	
116	Skip this section unless you need to route downstream paths based on the *response content* (e.g., `items.length > 0` vs empty). Do **not** use `branches` just to handle call failures — for that, use the `error` port (see [Wire edges](#wire-edges)).
117	
118	Each branch entry creates a `branch-{id}` source port. `$self` refers to the current HTTP node's output inside the condition.
119	
120	Set `branches` at `node add` time via `--input` (see [Add the node](#add-the-node)) — `branches` lives at `inputs.branches`, not `inputs.detail.branches`, and `node configure --detail` does not accept it.
121	
122	```bash
123	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
124	  --label "<HTTP node label>" \
125	  --input '{
126	    "branches": [
127	      { "id": "hasItems", "name": "Has Items", "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length > 0" },
128	      { "id": "empty",    "name": "Empty",    "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length == 0" }
129	    ]
130	  }' --output json
131	```
132	
133	> **Do not prefix `conditionExpression` with `=js:`** — HTTP branch conditions are auto-evaluated as JS (same rule as decision/switch expressions).
134	
135	### Wire edges
136	
137	The managed HTTP node's target port is `input`. Its source ports are:
138	
139	- `default` — primary success output (or fallback when configured branches don't match)
140	- `error` — fires when the HTTP call fails (network error, timeout, non-2xx not caught by a branch); wire this to an error handler to keep the flow from faulting
141	- `branch-{id}` — one per entry in `inputs.branches` ([Conditional branches](#conditional-branches)); use the exact `id` you set
142	
143	Use `Edit` to add edge objects to `edges[]`; do not use `uip maestro flow edge add` for this structural wiring. Examples:
144	
145	```json
146	{
147	  "id": "e-<upstreamNodeId>-<nodeId>",
148	  "sourceNodeId": "<upstreamNodeId>",
149	  "sourcePort": "<port>",
150	  "targetNodeId": "<nodeId>",
151	  "targetPort": "input"
152	}
153	```
154	
155	```json
156	{
157	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<downstreamNodeId>",
158	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
159	  "sourcePort": "default",
160	  "targetNodeId": "<downstreamNodeId>",
161	  "targetPort": "input"
162	}
163	```
164	
165	```json
166	{
167	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<errorHandlerId>",
168	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
169	  "sourcePort": "error",
170	  "targetNodeId": "<errorHandlerId>",
171	  "targetPort": "input"
172	}
173	```
174	
175	Add the `error` edge above **only when the requirements say what should happen if the call fails.** With no error edge, a failed call faults the flow — the correct, visible default.
176	
177	When an HTTP node does have an outgoing `error` edge, the HTTP node instance must also include `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true`. `uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set this automatically; direct JSON edits must set it explicitly. Never set the flag on an HTTP node with no error edge — it suppresses the fault, so a failed call flows on and the run reports success. See [file-format.md — Default: off](../../../../shared/file-format.md#default-off--enable-only-for-a-failure-the-flow-actually-handles).
178	
179	```json
180	{
181	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<hasItemsDownstream>",
182	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
183	  "sourcePort": "branch-hasItems",
184	  "targetNodeId": "<hasItemsDownstream>",
185	  "targetPort": "input"
186	}
187	```
188	
189	### Debug
190	
191	| Error | Cause | Fix |
192	| --- | --- | --- |
193	| `not_authed` or 401/403 | Wrong node type (v1 instead of v2), missing bindings, or expired connection | Verify node type is `core.action.http.v2`, check `bindings_v2.json` exists, ping the connection |
194	| `configuration` field missing | Node not configured via CLI | Run `uip maestro flow node configure` — do not hand-write `inputs.detail` |
195	| `flow validate` errors with `uiPathActivityTypeId` missing on `core.action.http.v2` | Node was hand-authored in `definitions[]` instead of via `uip maestro flow node add` | Remove the node, re-add it via `uip maestro flow node add <file> core.action.http.v2 ...`, then re-run `node configure`. |
196	| Connection not found | Wrong connection ID or connector key | Re-run `uip is connections list` for the target connector |
197	| Wrong API response | Incorrect `url` or `query` | Check the target service's API documentation |
198	| `ImplicitConnection` errors | Manual mode misconfigured | Verify `authentication: "manual"` and `url` is a full URL |
199	| Flow faults on 4xx/5xx response | No `error` edge wired from the HTTP node | Expected when the requirements specify no fallback. If they do, add an edge with `sourcePort: "error"` to an error-handler node. See [Implicit error port on action nodes](../../../../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes) — same mechanism applies to all action nodes |
200	| Flow reports `Completed` but the API call failed | `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true` with no handler, or an `error` edge routed into the happy path / the success End node | Remove the flag when there is no error edge; otherwise repoint the error edge at a distinct End node with an error/status output, or at `core.logic.terminate`. See [Do not swallow the failure](../../../../shared/file-format.md#do-not-swallow-the-failure) |
201	| Edge `source-port output` rejected | Referencing the variable namespace as a port name | HTTP source ports are `default`, `error`, and `branch-{id}` — not `output`. The `output` name is only a variable namespace (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) |

1	# HTTP Request Node — Connector Mode
2	
3	Use this walkthrough when the target service has an IS connector and you want managed auth (OAuth / API key) handled by an existing IS connection.
4	
5	**Prerequisite:** a healthy IS connection for the target connector. Step 2 verifies this. If none exists, propose manual mode as the fallback and confirm the switch with the user before finalizing — do not switch modes without that confirmation.
6	
7	Before starting, read [impl.md](impl.md) for the node type, registry validation, and the "always use `node configure`" rule. Follow Steps 1–5 in order.
8	
9	## Step 1 — Add the node
10	
11	```bash
12	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
13	  --label "<HTTP node label>" --output json
14	```
15	
16	> **Inside a loop body?** Add `--parent <LOOP_NODE_ID>` to set `parentId`. Without it, the node runs outside the loop context and outputs are null. See [loop/impl.md](../loop/impl.md).
17	
18	The CLI copies the manifest into `definitions[]`, adds the node instance, registers `variables.nodes`, and inserts a `layout.nodes` placeholder — byte-for-byte from the registry. Save the returned `<nodeId>` — Steps 2 and 3 reuse it. Leave `inputs` empty; Step 3 populates `inputs.detail`. Do not hand-author the definition — see [impl.md — Add the node](impl.md#add-the-node).
19	
20	## Step 2 — Identify target connection
21	
22	**Connector mode only works if the connector supports the HTTP request activity** — verify by running `uip is connectors get "<target-connector-key>"` and checking the `HasHttpRequest` flag. If the flag is false, **STOP** — a connection cannot help. Use the recovery question below (switch to manual mode / skip / something else; the create-a-connection option does not apply) and do not switch modes without confirmation.
23	
24	```bash
25	uip is connections list "<target-connector-key>" --all-folders --output json
26	```
27	
28	`--all-folders` is mandatory for discovery. Selection rules, empty-result recovery, and ping verification live in the platform skill — do not duplicate them here.
29	
30	> **MUST READ before any `uip is connections ...` call:** [/uipath:uipath-platform — connections.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/connections.md).
31	
32	Record the chosen connection's `Id` and `FolderKey` — Step 3 needs both.
33	
34	> **HTTP-specific recovery — no usable connection.** If platform-skill recovery yields nothing (empty after `--all-folders` + `--refresh`, user declines to create one), the HTTP node has unique fallback options. Ask the user to confirm the path — **manual mode is the recommended auto-fallback**, pre-selected, since it unblocks the node without a connection:
35	>
36	> - **Switch this node to manual mode** *(recommended)* — abandon this walkthrough and follow [impl-manual.md](impl-manual.md). Manual changes the auth model (you supply auth yourself), so this needs explicit confirmation.
37	> - **Create a new connection now** — `uip is connections create "<target-connector-key>"` starts the OAuth flow. User completes browser auth themselves, then re-run `uip is connections list` to pick up the new connection.
38	> - **Skip this node**.
39	> - **Something else**.
40	>
41	> Auto-try the fallback, but do not finalize a mode switch without the user's confirmation; do not invent a placeholder ID; do not skip the node without explicit selection. See the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../../../SKILL.md).
42	
43	## Step 3 — Configure the node
44	
45	> **STOP — open the platform skill before configuring.** Before composing `url` / `query` / `body`, read [/uipath:uipath-platform — http-request.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/http-request.md) and resolve every value you don't already have (IDs from names, required body fields, endpoint path, response shape).
46	>
47	> - **If the target connector is listed in that skill's `vendor-docs-registry.json`:** you MUST follow its **Step 0 (Ground Against the Vendor's API Docs)** — read the `docsUrl` + `notes` and confirm the exact endpoint with the `http-request` probe before running `node configure`. Pass the endpoint path verbatim: vendor method names can contain literal dots (Slack ``chat.postMessage`) — the dot is part of the path segment.
48	> - **If the connector is NOT listed:** the registry-grounding step does not apply — resolve missing values via the `http-request` probe / vendor docs as usual.
49	
50	```bash
51	uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <nodeId> \
52	  --detail '{
53	    "authentication": "connector",
54	    "targetConnector": "<target-connector-key>",
55	    "connectionId": "<target-connection-id>",
56	    "folderKey": "<folder-key>",
57	    "method": "GET",
58	    "url": "/api/endpoint",
59	    "query": {"param1": "value1"}
60	  }' --output json
61	```
62	
63	> **Connector mode supports `application/json` request and response bodies only.**
64	
65	The CLI:
66	
67	- Builds the full `inputs.detail` (connector, connectionId, bodyParameters, essentialConfiguration)
68	- Auto-fills both `bodyParameters.path` and `bodyParameters.url` from the single `url` value you pass
69	- Generates `bindings_v2.json`
70	- Creates a connection resource file under `resources/solution_folder/connection/`
71	
72	**Dynamic values:** connector input fields do not resolve `{$vars.x}` brace-templates — use `=js:` expressions for any dynamic `url` / `headers` / `body` / `query`. Pass the `=js:` string verbatim in `--detail`. Full rationale and examples: [impl.md — Dynamic values](impl.md#dynamic-values-in-url--headers--body--query).
73	
74	## Step 4 — (Optional) Response branches
75	
76	Skip unless you need to route downstream paths based on response content (e.g., `items.length > 0` vs empty). For generic call-failure handling use the `error` port in Step 5 instead. Full syntax and rules: [impl.md — Conditional branches](impl.md#conditional-branches).
77	
78	## Step 5 — Wire edges
79	
80	The HTTP node's target port is `input`. Source ports: `default` (success), `error` (network/non-2xx), `branch-{id}` (one per Step 4 entry). Wire `default` to the next node. Wire `error` to a handler **only when the requirements say what a failed call should do** — with no `error` edge the call faults the flow, which is the correct default, and setting `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true` without the edge swallows the failure into a run that reports success. See [file-format.md — Default: off](../../../../shared/file-format.md#default-off--enable-only-for-a-failure-the-flow-actually-handles).
81	
82	Edge JSON shapes and all four examples (upstream→node, default→downstream, error→handler, branch→downstream): [impl.md — Wire edges](impl.md#wire-edges).
83	
84	## Debug
85	
86	See [impl.md — Debug](impl.md#debug). For connector mode, the most common errors are `not_authed` / 401/403 (expired connection — ping it) and `Connection not found` (wrong connector key or connection ID — re-list).

1	# Managed HTTP Request - Concept + `http-request` Authoring Helper
2	
3	This doc covers two things every agent authoring a Managed HTTP Request needs to know:
4	1. What Managed HTTP Request is, and the two modes it runs in.
5	2. How to use the `http-request` CLI command to fill in the values Managed HTTP Request needs.
6	
7	Consumers: Maestro Flow, Maestro BPMN, API Workflows, Case Management, etc. Each consumer surfaces Managed HTTP Request differently (as a node, an activity, a tool call, …) and uses its own type identifier and configuration schema - the concept and the rules below are the same. For the exact node/activity type identifier and how to configure it, see your consumer's own authoring docs.
8	
9	## What is Managed HTTP Request?
10	
11	A built-in way to make an HTTP call from a UiPath automation. Runs in two modes - **connector mode** and **manual mode**:
12	
13	| Mode | When | `url` | Auth |
14	|---|---|---|---|
15	| **Connector** | Connector exists for the vendor but the specific operation is not curated | **Relative** to the connection's vendor base URL | Applied automatically from the bound connection |
16	| **Manual** | No connector exists, or public API with no auth needed | **Full URL** | You supply all headers, including auth |
17	
18	## Connector-Mode Rules
19	
20	- **Connector mode only works if the connector supports HTTP request activity** — verify by running `uip is connectors get "<connector-key>"` and checking the `HasHttpRequest` flag.
21	- `url` must be **relative**. Wrong: `"url": "https://example.atlassian.net/rest/api/2/issue"`. Right: `"url": "/issue"`.
22	- The connection's base URL is prepended automatically.
23	- The auth header is applied automatically - do not set `Authorization`.
24	- **`application/json` only - request and response.** No other content type is supported. File upload/download operations are the most common violation (`multipart/form-data`, `application/octet-stream`, binary/stream responses) - check the operation's request and response content types before authoring. If non-JSON, connector mode cannot call it - use a curated connector activity; if none exists, surface to the user.
25	- Get the exact vendor base URL for a connection via (so you can compose the relative `url` correctly):
26	
27	```bash
28	uip is connections base-url "<connection-id>" --output json
29	# → { "Data": { "BaseUrl": "https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/<site>/rest/api/2" } }
30	```
31	
32	## Manual-Mode Rules
33	
34	- `url` is the **fully qualified URL**.
35	- No connection is bound - you supply everything needed to make the call: URL, headers (including auth if needed), query params, and body.
36	
37	## Step 0: Ground Against the Vendor's API Docs (registry) — connector mode only
38	
39	> **Connector mode only.** This grounding step applies when `authentication: "connector"` (a connector exists and the `url` is **relative** to its vendor base URL). Manual mode targets an arbitrary REST API with a full URL and has no connector to look up — skip this step for manual mode.
40	
41	**Before composing any `url` / `query` / `body`, ground the endpoint against the vendor's documentation.** Skipping this is the most common cause of a wrong-but-plausible endpoint that still "completes" at runtime (many vendors return HTTP 200 with an error body for an unknown path — e.g. Slack `{"ok":false,"error":"unknown_method"}` — so a bad path does not fault).
42	
43	1. Look the target connector up in [`vendor-docs-registry.json`](vendor-docs-registry.json) (same directory). Match by `connectorKey`.
44	2. **If listed:** read its `docsUrl` (authoritative API reference) and `notes` (vendor-specific conventions: endpoint shape, custom-field keys, query quirks). Honor the `notes` verbatim, then confirm the exact path with the `http-request` probe below (the live call is the final authority — the registry only grounds the baseline).
45	3. **If NOT listed:** this registry-grounding step does not apply. Proceed with the normal authoring flow — resolve the endpoint and any missing values via the `http-request` probe below, as you would otherwise.
46	
47	> **Pass endpoint paths verbatim — do NOT "REST-ify" them.** Many vendor APIs name operations with **literal dots**, where the whole dotted token is a single path segment: Slack`chat.postMessage`, `conversations.replies`. The dot is **not** a namespace separator — never rewrite `chat.postMessage` as `/chat/postMessage`. Copy the method exactly as the docs/registry show it (`"url": "/chat.postMessage"`).
48	
49	## Authoring Helper: `http-request` command
50	
51	Authoring a Managed HTTP Request payload requires concrete vendor values - IDs, field names, endpoint paths. Use `http-request` command to call any vendor API directly through the connection - same auth, same base URL the Managed HTTP Request will use at runtime.
52	
53	### When the Agent Needs `http-request` command
54	
55	Use `http-request` command to resolve any of the following before authoring the Managed HTTP Request payload:
56	
57	- **Identifier lookups.** Resolve a human-friendly name to the vendor's internal ID. Examples: project key from a project name, channel ID from a channel name, user ID from email/name, custom-field IDs.
58	- **Required and optional fields** the vendor expects in the request body
59	- **Endpoint paths, query params, pagination tokens** before committing to a payload
60	- **Vendor error responses** for unsupported parameters or permissions
61	
62	### Command
63	
64	```bash
65	uip is resources run create "<connector-key>" http-request \
66	  --connection-id "<id>" \
67	  --body '{"method":"<method>","url":"<relative-path>"}' --output json
68	```
69	
70	| `body` field | Required | Notes |
71	|---|---|---|
72	| `method` | Yes | Uppercase HTTP verb |
73	| `url` | Yes | **Relative** to the connection's vendor base URL (same convention as Managed HTTP Request connector mode) |
74	| `headers` | No | Extra headers. Do NOT set `Authorization`. |
75	| `body` | For POST/PUT/PATCH | **Stringified** JSON. Only `application/json` is supported today — no other content type. |
76	
77	`http-request` command uses the same connection that Managed HTTP Request will use at runtime, so auth + base URL are applied automatically - same convention as Managed HTTP Request itself.
78	
79	### Read-Only During Authoring
80	
81	When using the `http-request` command, use `GET` method only, as `POST` / `PATCH` / `PUT` / `DELETE` mutate vendor state, often irreversibly.
82	
83	Exception: the user asks you to actually run the operation now, not just author it.
84	
85	## Worked Example: Jira Create Issue
86	
87	User wants to create a Jira issue. Before composing the Managed HTTP Request payload, the agent needs the project key, issue type ID, and required custom fields. All resolved via `http-request` command GETs.
88	
89	```bash
90	# 1. Resolve project key (user said "Engineering project").
91	uip is resources run create uipath-atlassian-jira http-request \
92	  --connection-id "<id>" \
93	  --body '{"method":"GET","url":"/project/search?query=Engineering"}' --output json
94	# → key "ENG"
95	
96	# 2. For project ENG, get available issue types + required custom fields.
97	uip is resources run create uipath-atlassian-jira http-request \
98	  --connection-id "<id>" \
99	  --body '{"method":"GET","url":"/issue/createmeta?projectKeys=ENG&expand=projects.issuetypes.fields"}' \
100	  --output json
101	# → match "Task" → id "10001"; required custom field: customfield_10010 (Story Points)
102	```
103	
104	3. (Optional) Confirm resolved values with the user.
105	
106	4. Compose the Managed HTTP Request payload. The actual configuration command and schema are consumer-specific — the request body Managed HTTP Request will send to Jira at runtime looks like:
107	
108	```json
109	{
110	  "method": "POST",
111	  "url": "/issue",
112	  "body": {
113	    "fields": {
114	      "project": { "key": "ENG" },
115	      "issuetype": { "id": "10001" },
116	      "summary": "Fix coder evals",
117	      "customfield_10010": 3
118	    }
119	  }
120	}
121	```
122	
123	All steps 1-2 are GETs because we are in the authoring phase. The POST to `/issue` happens at runtime, performed by Managed HTTP Request - never by CLI during authoring.
124	
125	## Critical Rules
126	
127	1. **Do NOT set the `Authorization` header manually in connector mode.** Auth is applied automatically by the connection. Setting it yourself can leak or override the token.
128	2. **Do NOT use an absolute URL in connector-mode `url`.** Wrong: `"url": "https://example.atlassian.net/rest/api/2/project"`. Right: `"url": "/project"`.
129	3. **Do NOT issue writes via CLI during authoring.** See "Read-Only During Authoring" above.
130	4. **Do NOT guess the base URL.** Use `uip is connections base-url <connection-id>`.
131	5. **(Connector mode) Ground the endpoint before authoring.** Look the vendor up in [`vendor-docs-registry.json`](vendor-docs-registry.json), read its `docsUrl` + `notes`, and confirm the path with the `http-request` probe. See [Step 0](#step-0-ground-against-the-vendors-api-docs-registry--connector-mode-only).
132	6. **(Connector mode) Pass endpoint paths verbatim.** 
133	7. **In connector mode, request and response bodies are `application/json` only.** No other content type is supported; do NOT set `Content-Type` to anything else. Same rule applies to the `http-request` helper command body (it runs through a connection). Manual mode has no such limit — you supply your own `Content-Type` and body.
134
